title: DMS and change data capture out of a legacy database

videos.script: Quitanda's shop still runs on the PostgreSQL it started with, and orders arrive in it every minute. Moving it is the problem of this lesson. {{shop}} Copying the tables takes hours, and the shop will not stop for hours. So a migration has two halves. Copy what is there, then keep up with what keeps changing. {{halves}} The second half is change data capture. Every database writes its changes to a log before it applies them, and CDC reads that log from outside. {{log}} DMS does both halves. You will build its instance, its endpoints and a task in the lab, and see exactly what moto pretends. {{dms}} Then the real thing. A PostgreSQL server on your own machine, a replication slot, and the inserts, updates and deletes coming out of its log as you make them. {{slot}} You will also see the slot's danger. Stop reading it, and the old database keeps its log until the disk fills. {{danger}} And at the end, the cutover, in the order that loses nothing, and what the migration costs by the hour. {{end}}
